title: Observability debt reduction & cost-triage roadmap (2027)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This roadmap captures a coordinated 12-month program to pay down observability debt across the platform, align alerting to product-critical SLIs, and create a persistent cost-triage process that recovers at least $120k/month of avoidable telemetry spend by EOY 2027. The goal is fewer noisy alerts, more actionable dashboards, and lower telemetry spend while preserving signal for incidents and outages.

Context and motivation:
- Over the last 18 months we added many debug metrics and high-cardinality spans to accelerate feature delivery. That increased signal availability but produced: noisy alerts (alert fatigue), unsized dashboards, expensive storage/ingestion costs, and brittle SLI coverage where key services lack business-aligned metrics.
- Platform teams and oncall operators report a "noise tax" that slows response and drives misprioritization. Finance has flagged observability spend as an optimization target for next budget cycle.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: alert rationalization, dashboard consolidation, metric cardinality limits, retention policy rationalization, automated cost-triage runbook, and platform-level guardrails for new telemetry.
- Out of scope: wholesale vendor migration, application feature telemetry design (we will consult app owners but not redesign app metrics), or full tracing rearchitecture.

Program goals (SMART):
1) Reduce actionable alert volume for platform-wide oncall by 45% (alerts/person/day) by 2027-09-30.
2) Recover $120k/month in telemetry spend through retention, sampling, and cardinality fixes by 2027-12-31.
3) Increase business-aligned SLI coverage to 95% of production traffic paths by 2027-06-30.
4) Deploy automated cost-triage playbook and dashboard for continuous monitoring by 2027-03-31.

Key metrics and definitions (will be instrumented in the observability dashboard):
- Observability Debt Score (ODS): composite 0-100 score per service computed from: redundant metrics, high-cardinality metric count, orphan dashboards, and stale alerts. Lower is better.
- Alert Noise Ratio (ANR): ratio of alerts acknowledged without escalation to total alerts (target <= 0.3).
- Telemetry Spend Recovered: monthly $ reclaimed after policy/pruning changes.
- SLI Coverage Ratio: percent of production request paths mapped to at least one business SLI with alerting.

Quarterly milestones (program-level):
- Q1 2027 (triage & pilot):
  - Run full inventory of metrics/spans/dashboards/alerts for top 25 services by traffic and spend.
  - Launch cost-triage dashboard and a weekly "telemetry sprints" cadence with service owners.
  - Pilot retention and sampling changes on two low-risk services (billing-api, metrics-ingest).
- Q2 2027 (scale & SLI alignment):
  - Implement platform-level cardinality guardrail: denylist and per-tenant tag quotas.
  - Map and create business SLIs for all services in the top-25 list; add SLI health panels.
  - Run alert ownership cleanup: reassign or close stale alerts (>90 days w/o hits).
- Q3 2027 (automation & cost recovery):
  - Roll out automated telemetry trimming for metrics with 0 reads in 90 days.
  - Integrate cost-triage alerts into cost ops Slack channel and billing dashboards.
  - Measure first 60% of target spend recovery.
- Q4 2027 (hardening & guardrails):
  - Ship telemetry onboarding checklist and CI gating for new metrics/dashboards.
  - Reduce alert noise by 45% and reach telemetry spend target $120k/month.
  - Retrospective and postmortem of program impact with next-year roadmap.

Implementation details and design patterns:
- Inventory process: use a combination of vendor APIs (metrics list, dashboard list) and the platform telemetry indexer to produce canonical lists by service tag. Inventory output schema (CSV) will include: service, metric_name, cardinality_estimate, created_at, last_query, owner.

- Observability Debt Score (calculation sketch):
  - redundant_metric_penalty = unique_metrics_duplicated / unique_metrics_total * 40
  - high_cardinality_penalty = min(30, summed_cardinality_score)
  - stale_alert_penalty = stale_alerts_count * 1.5
  - orphan_dashboard_penalty = orphan_dashboards_count * 0.8
  - ODS = round(redundant_metric_penalty + high_cardinality_penalty + stale_alert_penalty + orphan_dashboard_penalty, 1)

- Cardinality and sampling policy (examples):
  - Platform default: tag cardinality limit = 2 tags with 50 unique values each (enforced by SDK instrumentation hook).
  - High-cardinality signals must use sketches/sampled histograms.
  - Server-side sampling for spans: 10% default with header to opt-up for debugging.

Dashboards & alerts changes (developer-facing guidance):
- Dashboards:
  - Consolidate: combine related low-use dashboards into a single service overview per team. Each overview must have: 1 business SLI, 2 platform health metrics (CPU/GPU/queue depth), 1 error-class breakdown, 1 latency P95/P99 panel.
  - Metadata: every dashboard must include owner, last-maintained date, and a short purpose paragraph. Dashboards without an owner for >60 days go into an "orphaned" list and will be scheduled for removal.

- Alerting policy (practical rules):
  - Avoid single-metric static thresholds unless tied to SLI burns. Prefer rate-based and composite alerts.
  - For alerts with >10% false-positive rate, require a remediation plan or disablement within 14 days.
  - All high-severity alerts (P0/P1) require a linked runbook and an assigned responder within the alert definition.

Example alert rule (YAML sketch to add to platform alert templates):
---
name: "service.http.error-rate-high"
expr: "sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"SERVICE\",status=~\"5..\"}[5m])) by (service) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"SERVICE\"}[5m])) by (service) > 0.02"
for: "5m"
labels:
  severity: "P1"
annotations:
  runbook: "/runbooks/service-http-error-rate-high"
  owner: "@service-oncall"
---

Cost-triage runbook (high-level):
1) Alert fires into #cost-triage Slack and creates a ticket in the Telemetry backlog with tag "cost-triage".
2) Run inventory query: list all metrics/spans/dashboards contributing to the spike.
3) If the top contributor is high-cardinality metric: set a quick sampling rule and create a remediation PR.
4) If the top contributor is retention or export: temporarily reduce retention to 7 days for the metric group and notify stakeholders.
5) Validate impact on alerting and SLIs; rollback if SLI deviation > 0.5%.

Rollout plan and migration steps (detailed):
- Week 0-4: communication and training: recorded demos, office hours, and OnePager for teams.
- Week 4-12: inventory + pilot fixes (two pilot services).
- Week 12-20: expand to top-25 services and implement cardinality guardrail in SDK.
- Week 20-36: platform automation for metric pruning and retention enforcement.
- Week 36-52: CI gating for new telemetry and program retrospective.

Ownership, RACI, and operating model:
- Program lead: Aisha Patel (platform observability) — overall delivery, stakeholder coordination.
- Engineering owners: each service owner — responsible for implementing fixes for their service.
- Platform SRE: Diego Ramirez — enforcement of guardrails, SDK changes, CI gating.
- Cost ops / FinOps: Sophie Chen — validation of spend recovered and billing integration.
- Platform product manager: Liam O'Connor — prioritization and roadmap alignment.

Dependencies and risks:
- Dependency: vendor APIs must support metric listing and query history export. If absent, we will build lightweight exporters but schedule slips possible.
- Risk: removing metrics may break downstream dashboards or 3rd-party integrations. Mitigation: staged pruning with a 14-day tombstone mode (metrics hidden from dashboards but retained for rollback).
- Risk: SLI regressions from aggressive sampling. Mitigation: pre-change SLI impact simulation in the sandbox environment and strict rollback criteria (SLI deviation >0.5%).

Budget and resourcing ask (FY27):
- Headcount: 0.4 FTE platform-engineer dedicated Q1-Q4; 0.6 FTE SRE Q2-Q4; 0.2 PM.
- One-time infra investment: $45k for automation scripts and retention tooling.
- Expected monthly savings: phased to $40k/month by Q3 and $120k/month by Q4.

Success criteria and acceptance tests:
- Program acceptance checklist:
  - ODS reduced by >=35 points on average across top-25 services.
  - Alert Noise Ratio <=0.3 for platform oncall.
  - Telemetry spend reduction >=$120k/month on billing reports.
  - 95% SLI coverage for production paths.

Monitoring, cadence, and retrospective plan:
- Weekly telemetry sprints for the first 12 weeks.
- Monthly executive check-ins for finance and product.
- Quarterly retrospective to capture lessons, update guardrails, and seed next-year roadmap.

Appendices and references:
- Appendix A: Inventory CSV schema (column list): service, metric_name, type, cardinality_estimate, last_query_ts, owner, created_ts, retention_days.
- Appendix B: Example Terraform/CI check (pseudo):
  - if new_metric then assert(metadata.owner != null and metadata.purpose != null and cardinality_estimate <= PLATFORM_MAX)
- Links: see related pages above for token-cost attribution and cache prefetching guidance.

Open questions for leadership:
- What is the acceptable SLI deviation threshold for temporary telemetry pruning during cost incidents? (default proposed: 0.5%)
- Approve $45k one-time tooling budget and headcount fractions in FY27 plan.

Contact and next steps:
- Program kickoff scheduled 2027-01-10. Questions or comments: contact Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) or Diego Ramirez (diego@redwood.ai).
